It was a worthwhile battle for the Russians but I am pretty sure after a time there wasn't lines out the door for volunteers anymore. It's novel to think of battle as being so glorious that if its "worth it" people will step forward to support the cause. War is hell though not some glorious fantasy. If you and all those that you knew were being mowed down by the thousands though, I'm sure those lines of volunteers would dry up pretty damn fast. Now lets put ourselves in a similar situation here in the US but instead of a Draft or some form of Selective Service we just give people to option not to fight. How long would our country stand? Wars like the Vietnam War make it a little more conflicting and I can see those arguments for being against the Draft. However, it's a double edged sword... If you turn the tables and apply the same theory, it becomes a little more obvious why we have things like Selective Service. I would also argue that we have come a long way from the Draft, but, things like going to college should not exempt people from having to serve in their countries time of need. I see college as a privilege but Freedom is our right. Perhaps there is some middle ground, but, abolishing all forms of service requirements is ludicrous. A lot of countries have mandatory service requirements already while we simply get put on a list for a few years. It could be better but it could also be a hell of a lot worse.
